chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying concerning the one who has fainted: He said: Whatever Allah has overcome him with, then Allah is more entitled to excuse for it.

key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One whose decree encompasses the condition mentioned
key_terms.الْعُذْرِ: excuse or exemption due to incapacity
key_terms.الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: the person who has lost consciousness or fainted
key_terms.غَلَبَ: overcame or overtook beyond one’s control

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on religious duty for a person who becomes unconscious?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a person overcome by unconsciousness. It states that when a condition is imposed upon someone beyond his control, Allah is most entitled to grant excuse, indicating leniency in religious obligation in such a case.
